terms.definition: A group of cells with a similar structure and function.
terms.examiner: Cells, tissues, organs, organ systems, organism: know the order.

terms.definition: A group of tissues that perform a specific function, such as the stomach.
terms.examiner: The stomach contains muscular, glandular and epithelial tissue.

terms.definition: A biological catalyst: a protein that speeds up a reaction without being used up.
terms.examiner: Enzymes have an active site with a specific shape.

terms.definition: The part of an enzyme where the substrate fits and the reaction happens.
terms.examiner: Lock and key model: only a substrate with the complementary shape fits.

terms.definition: The active site has changed shape, so the substrate no longer fits and the enzyme cannot work. Caused by high temperature or extreme pH.
terms.examiner: Do not say the enzyme is "killed": it is not alive.

terms.definition: An enzyme that breaks carbohydrates into simple sugars; amylase breaks starch into sugars.
terms.examiner: Amylase is made in the salivary glands, pancreas and small intestine.

terms.definition: An enzyme that breaks proteins into amino acids.
terms.examiner: Made in the stomach (pepsin), pancreas and small intestine.

terms.definition: An enzyme that breaks lipids into fatty acids and glycerol.
terms.examiner: Made in the pancreas and small intestine.

terms.definition: Made in the liver and stored in the gall bladder; it is alkaline, neutralising stomach acid, and it emulsifies fats into small droplets, increasing their surface area.
